sections.title: Growth and stems
sections.text: Rhipsalis paradoxa is an epiphytic cactus native to southeastern and southern Brazil. Its long, hanging shoots can reach about 5 m; their stiff, three-angled segments join in a distinctive zigzag chain.

sections.title: Flowers and fruit
sections.text: Small white, radially symmetrical flowers, about 1–2 cm across, grow singly from the areoles. The globose fruits are pale or translucent when ripe.

sections.title: Image comparison
sections.text: The plate accurately shows the pendant chains of three-winged segments and white flowers. It does not establish an edible use for the fruit.
